JUDGEMENT CALLS
  S6 (431,450) deg4 -> CROSSING (overrode the tracer's junction default). inkmap shows the vertical wire sitting at x~425 above the rail, bulging diagonally out to x~433 exactly at the rail, then returning to x~422 below: a drawn sideways jog (tracer hop score 3.6, the highest on the sheet), and no solder blob (dot 2.2 - same as ordinary strokes; compare the unmistakable blob at S2, dot 3.1). Reading it as a junction would merge n2 into n3, i.e. tie the gate of MOSFET-N #1 to its own source AND to the source of MOSFET-P #3 and the drain of #5 - #1 would be permanently off and the V-AC #7 branch would lose its own node.
  S12 (429,534) deg4 -> CROSSING, same evidence: vertical at x~421 above, bulging to x~430 at the rail, back to x~418 below; hop 3.6, dot 2.1. As a junction it would merge n2 into n4, shorting the gate of MOSFET-N #9 to its own drain and to the gate of MOSFET-P #3. With both S6 and S12 left at the default the tracer produced a single 10-terminal net that shorted gate-to-source on three separate MOSFETs - electrically degenerate, so the jog reading is the only sane one.
  All other CRITICAL sites (S1,S2,S5,S9,S11,S13,S14,S16,S31,S33,S34,S35) are plain T's - a wire terminating on a through-running wire - and are recorded as junctions after looking at each crop. S2 additionally carries a real solder blob.
  Non-critical sites S3,S4,S17,S19,S23,S24,S26 are handwriting ('5V','3V','1kOhm','2kHz','5A','1A') brushing a wire; S21 is the elbow on the gate lead of #9. None changes the netlist; left at default.

NOTE ON DRAIN-vs-SOURCE
  For all five MOSFETs the drawn symbol settles it: the body/arrow stub is tied to the lower lead, so the lower lead is the source and the upper lead the drain. I used the ink rather than the physical rail-position heuristic, and they disagree for #3 (a P-channel whose drain, not source, faces the +5V top rail) and #5 - these are randomly generated netlists, so that is expected and I did not 'fix' it.
